newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-South Australian defence firms form alliances.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-South Australian defence firms form alliances.

text.p: About 30 South Australian defence companies, including British Aerospace Australia, have formed an alliance to win major Australian and offshore projects, the State Government said on Wednesday.

Speaking at the launch of the Defence Teaming Centre (DFC) alliance, Industry Minister John Olsen said the state wanted to win more than 40 percent of an anticipated A$30 billion in federal spending on defence projects over the next 10-15 years.

The alliance, the Defence Teaming Centre (DTC), had negotiated a memorandum of understanding with the United States Defence and Space Consortium (DSC) and attracted interest from major US defence and aerospace companies, he said.
Olsen said critical mass had been reached in the SA defence industry, which currently won about 40 percent of Australian defence procurement dollars.

"The DTC will assist member companies break into new markets and win projects that were previously out of reach because of limitations caused by size and individual capability," he said in a statement.

Supported by key State and federal research and development agencies, the DTC comprised some of the State's biggest defence companies, including BAeA, Vision Abell, and CelsiusTech Australia, he said.

"Over the next 10-15 years, an estimated A$30 billion worth of defence projects are expected to be proffered for tender by the Australian Defence Force and South Australian companies have a good chance of winning a considerable proportion of this work," he said.

South Australia is base for a number of major national defence projects, including the contruction of the Collins Class submarines and operational support centre for the Jindalee over-the-horizon radar network.
